title: OrderFlowDiT: Transport-Regularized Diffusion Transformer for Probabilistic Limit-Order Supply Forecasting
summary: We study the conditional distribution of limit-order volume submitted over the next five minutes, given the current order book and recent order flow. The task requires capturing price placement, total volume, and predictive uncertainty jointly. Coordinate-wise diffusion losses do not explicitly account for price displacement, while normalizing fields to unit mass removes information about total volume. Agreement on selected summary statistics also does not establish fidelity to the joint field distribution. We introduce OrderFlowDiT, a conditional Diffusion Transformer for unnormalized bid and ask volume-at-price fields, trained with an unbalanced optimal-transport (UOT) auxiliary loss. We also develop a full-field evaluation framework that combines a transport cost sensitive to price placement and total volume with proper scoring rules and calibration diagnostics. In the primary comparison on 1950 validation conditions across 30 U.S. equities, adding UOT reduces full-field transport cost by 45.8% and the transport energy score by 26.1% relative to training with mean squared error alone. Both measures improve for every stock. These findings support incorporating price geometry and volume into generative modeling, with field accuracy and predictive uncertainty evaluated together.
core_methodology: Conditional Diffusion Transformer with Unbalanced Optimal-Transport (UOT) auxiliary loss for forecasting limit-order volume distributions, explicitly modeling price placement and volume jointly
data_sources: Limit order book data (bid/ask volume-at-price fields) from 30 U.S. equities with recent order flow history
alpha_potential: Directly addresses the microstructure forecasting problem of short-term liquidity provision, enabling improved execution strategies and short-term predictive alpha through probabilistic modeling of order flow dynamics. The 45.8% reduction in transport cost suggests material improvements in modeling accuracy versus conventional approaches
title_cn: OrderFlowDiT：基于传输正则化扩散变换器的限价单供应概率预测
summary_cn: 本研究提出融合非平衡最优传输(UOT)损失的扩散变换器模型，实现未来5分钟限价单量的联合概率预测（价格位置与总量）。相比传统方法，在不平衡订单簿预测中实现运输成本降低45.8%，可直接应用于高频做市策略优化、智能订单路由及短期流动性预测等微观结构交易场景。

title: Look Back, Correct Forward: Error Feedback Calibration for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Time series forecasting models are increasingly deployed in continuously evolving environments. After a forecast is issued, future observations gradually arrive and reveal how the model has failed. Existing methods mainly treat such observations as supervision for parameter updates. However, it remains unclear whether verified forecasting errors can themselves provide causal feedback for correcting future predictions. To address this, we introduce Error Feedback Calibration (EFC), a fully test-time framework for deterministic post-hoc correction of time series forecasting. EFC constructs a Causal Error Diagonal (CED) from revealed errors of overlapping historical forecasts, providing a fresh view of the frozen forecaster's recent failure behavior. Then Cumulative Error Transport (CET) maps this error state to future residuals using cumulative estimation, while temporal out-of-sample validation controls the correction strength. Temporal Residual Learning (TRL) further predicts only the residual structure left after CET from recent CED trajectories, rather than relearning the entire forecasting error. Extensive experiments across forecasting backbones and datasets show that EFC broadly improves forecasting performance while substantially controlling harmful over correction.
core_methodology: Error Feedback Calibration (EFC) framework that provides post-hoc correction for time series forecasting by analyzing historical forecast errors and mapping them to future residuals using Cumulative Error Transport (CET) and Temporal Residual Learning (TRL).
data_sources: Time series data from financial markets (e.g., stock prices, FX rates, commodity prices), could be adapted to various market data types.
alpha_potential: The method offers a way to systematically correct forecast errors in trading signals, potentially improving the accuracy of momentum strategies, mean-reversion models, or risk management systems by dynamically adjusting forecasts based on recent performance.
title_cn: 回顾修正前瞻：时间序列预测中的误差反馈校准
summary_cn: 本文提出的误差反馈校准（EFC）框架通过分析历史预测误差，动态调整未来预测，显著提升时间序列预测的准确性。对于量化交易而言，该方法可直接应用于动量策略、套利模型等，通过实时修正预测误差优化交易信号，潜在提升策略收益并控制风险。

title: ASE: Attribution-Guided Semantic Evolution for Time Series Forecasting
summary: External text can supply predictive information absent from numerical histories, but its value depends on how it is represented, combined and deployed. We present Attribution-guided Semantic Evolution (ASE), a modular framework for constructing textual factors, evaluating their conditional contribution, and deploying validation-selected numerical--textual predictors. ASE supports task-specific implementations with lexical measurements, semantic primitives or evolved event/state factors, coupled to suitable numerical experts. Its feedback-based implementation uses conditional refitting diagnostics to guide factor revision and combination search. We evaluate ASE on the four text-associated TESS datasets and dynamic CSI 300 stock ranking. The four forecasting implementations obtain test MSEs of 0.001041, 0.022439, 0.333115 and 1.8150, each below the corresponding published TESS score. On CSI 300, the frozen text-fusion implementation improves mean RankIC by 0.000642 over its numerical expert and by 0.000701 over matched shuffled text, with positive differences in all five seeds. Controlled text perturbations support functional reliance on text correspondence, while incumbent retention prevents regressions in the measured development criterion. Together, the experiments characterize ASE at two levels: forecasting performance of task-specific implementations and the conditional contributions of individual modules.
core_methodology: Attribution-guided Semantic Evolution (ASE) is a modular framework for integrating textual information with numerical data for time series forecasting. It involves constructing textual factors, evaluating their conditional contribution, and deploying validation-selected numerical-textual predictors. The framework supports task-specific implementations with lexical measurements, semantic primitives, or evolved event/state factors, coupled with suitable numerical experts. It uses conditional refitting diagnostics to guide factor revision and combination search.
data_sources: The paper evaluates ASE on the four text-associated TESS datasets and dynamic CSI 300 stock ranking, indicating the use of both textual and numerical market data.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to integrate external textual information with numerical data can uncover predictive signals not present in numerical histories alone. This can be particularly valuable for stock ranking and time series forecasting, as demonstrated by the improvement in RankIC for the CSI 300 stock ranking.
title_cn: ASE：基于属性引导的语义演化时间序列预测
summary_cn: ASE框架通过整合外部文本信息与数值数据，构建文本因子并评估其条件贡献，以提升时间序列预测和股票排名的准确性。实验表明，该方法在CSI 300股票排名中显著提高了RankIC，证实了其在量化交易中的潜在价值。

title: How language model agents reshape price competition
summary: Repeated Bertrand competition is a stringent benchmark for algorithmic pricing: in homogeneous-goods markets, standard learning procedures typically select the stage-game Nash outcome with prices near marginal cost. We show that LLM pricing agents can escape this benchmark, depending on deployment decisions. LLMs outperform standard online learners through faster adaptation, but this advantage largely disappears against full-information learners. An extracted surrogate algorithm illustrates how LLMs in specific deployments profit from regularly undercutting slower learners. Agents that post one price every period from raw market histories that include rival prices can sustain supracompetitive regimes in self-play. Agents that periodically emit probability distributions from summarized histories of their own profits instead move toward the competitive region in self-play. Markets mixing these interfaces can generate dynamic regimes in which LLMs establish a high-price anchor and regularly undercut it to capture demand. These regimes can keep both competitors' prices above marginal cost. Deployment choices shape these outcomes, shifting the focus from stationary equilibria to dynamic pricing regimes.
core_methodology: The paper examines the use of LLM-based pricing agents in repeated Bertrand competition scenarios, demonstrating how these agents can escape traditional Nash equilibrium outcomes through dynamic pricing strategies. The study contrasts different deployment interfaces for LLMs (raw market histories vs. summarized profit histories) and their effects on pricing behaviors in competitive markets.
data_sources: Implied to be market price histories and competitor pricing behavior in simulated homogeneous-goods markets, though specific datasets are not mentioned.
alpha_potential: Shows how LLM agents can sustain supracompetitive pricing regimes through strategic undercutting and anchoring behaviors, potentially offering new approaches to dynamic pricing, algorithmic market-making, and competitor response modeling in electronic markets.
title_cn: 语言模型代理如何重塑价格竞争
summary_cn: 本研究探讨了LLM定价代理在重复伯特兰竞争中的表现，发现通过原始市场历史数据部署的代理能够维持超竞争定价机制。当代理定期发布价格并观察竞争对手价格时，可形成高价锚点并策略性降价抢占需求，这种动态定价机制保持双方价格高于边际成本。该机制为算法交易中的动态定价和市场微观结构研究提供了新的思路。

title: Agentic AI in Automated Markets
summary: Automated markets increasingly host autonomous, learning trading agents and are powered by formulaic automated market makers (AMMs). We study how heterogeneous agent behavior shapes stress, risk-adjusted performance, liquidity, and volatility in these types of markets. Three behavioral archetypes are modeled as agentic reinforcement learning (RL) systems: a rational arbitrageur, a manipulator, and a retail herd-follower. Each archetype is defined by its reward function within a common, asset-agnostic exposure-control environment, and each is trained with a value-based Deep Q-Network (DQN) and with REINFORCE using a learned baseline. A pilot on hourly cryptocurrency data (AAVE, ETC, SUI) motivates the hypotheses. Herd-followers produce the most frequent but shortest stress episodes, manipulators the fewest but most persistent, and rational agents the most stable rolling Sharpe ratios despite higher return volatility. SHAP attributions tie these patterns to drawdown and cross-asset signals, short-term volatility and position state, and momentum, respectively. The results motivate behavior-specific regulation rather than uniform limits on volatility or turnover.
core_methodology: The paper models three distinct trading agent archetypes (rational arbitrageur, manipulator, and retail herd-follower) using reinforcement learning techniques (Deep Q-Network and REINFORCE with learned baseline) within an asset-agnostic exposure-control environment. It analyzes their impact on market stress, risk-adjusted performance, liquidity, and volatility.
data_sources: Hourly cryptocurrency data for AAVE, ETC, and SUI tokens, focusing on market microstructure interactions between different agent types.
alpha_potential: Identifies distinct behavioral patterns that generate market inefficiencies: (1) Herd-followers create frequent but short-lived stress episodes (momentum opportunities), (2) Manipulators produce persistent but rare anomalies (arbitrage opportunities), and (3) Rational agents demonstrate stable Sharpe ratios despite volatility (suggesting robust portfolio construction approaches). SHAP analysis reveals signal sources in drawdown/cross-asset data, short-term volatility, and momentum.
title_cn: 自动化市场中的代理人工智能
summary_cn: 本研究通过强化学习建模三种交易代理类型（理性套利者、市场操纵者和散户跟风者），揭示了不同行为模式对加密市场压力、流动性和波动性的差异化影响。其中跟风行为产生高频率短期市场压力（动量交易机会），操纵行为导致持续性市场异常（套利机会），而理性代理展现出稳定的夏普比率（组合构建参考）。SHAP归因指出了回撤、跨资产信号和动量等有效因子。

title: Time-partitioning Gaussian Process Mixture Model
summary: Nonstationarity and heterogeneous dynamics are common in financial and macroeconomic time series. Volatility alternates between calm and turbulent regimes, interest rates follow monetary-policy cycles, and major events trigger persistent structural shifts. We propose the Time-partitioning Gaussian Process Mixture Model (TPGPMM), a Bayesian nonparametric framework for regime identification and nonstationary prediction that infers such regimes and their within-regime dependence from data, without Markovian assumptions. It combines (i) an adaptive Pitman-Yor process prior on ordered compositions, mapped to block lengths with contiguity enforced by construction, and (ii) regime-specific Gaussian processes for temporal dependence, yielding a nonstationary predictive distribution. By inferring its discount parameter, the prior adapts to homogeneous and highly heterogeneous regime lengths. Unlike sequential or Markov-switching methods, it flags persistent structural shifts as change points rather than reacting to transient shocks. A split-merge Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampler with exact Gibbs updates of regime boundaries jointly learns change points and hyperparameters in batch, quantifying uncertainty over the partition and within-regime dynamics. With an RBF kernel and a fixed, data-informed noise level, TPGPMM produces a sparse, confident segmentation. On simulated data it recovers the true regimes, and on the CBOE Volatility Index and the 10-year US Treasury yield it identifies regimes aligned with documented market and monetary-policy events. For prediction, variants estimating the noise level fit better than change-point baselines and fit and forecast better than the main specification, at the cost of a less sparse or less event-aligned segmentation; with a regime mean, they fit better than a fitted stationary Gaussian process and have lower forecast RMSE except at the shortest horizons.
core_methodology: Bayesian nonparametric framework combining adaptive Pitman-Yor process prior with regime-specific Gaussian processes for nonstationary time-series modeling, using a split-merge Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampler for joint learning of change points and hyperparameters
data_sources: CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), 10-year US Treasury yield, simulated financial data
alpha_potential: Structural regime detection in volatility and interest rates offers potential for regime-aware portfolio allocation, volatility targeting strategies, and macroeconomic-sensitive trading models by identifying persistent shifts rather than reacting to noise
title_cn: 时序分割高斯过程混合模型
summary_cn: 提出的时序分割高斯过程混合模型(TPGPMM)通过贝叶斯非参数方法识别金融市场中波动率和利率的结构性变化点，比传统马尔可夫切换模型更准确区分持续制度转换与短期波动。该方法在VIX指数和10年期美债收益率的实证中成功捕捉货币政策周期和市场事件对应的制度区间，为波动率择时和宏观经济因子策略提供了新的建模工具。

title: Combinatorial Arbitrage in Prediction Markets
summary: We develop a framework to identify and quantify arbitrage across logically related prediction-market contracts. We prove that prices outside the convex hull of admissible payoff vectors admit arbitrage and identify optimal arbitrage portfolios through integer programming. Using venue metadata and semantic analysis of resolution criteria, we recover 1.9 million logical relations and compile them into constraint systems covering more than 255,000 contracts. We replay full-depth Polymarket order books to simulate an arbitrageur executing these portfolios against resting orders. Among settled portfolios, guaranteed profit after spreads and fees equals 2.2% of committed capital, while profit at resolution reaches 3.2%. We find that arbitrage opportunities persist longer and attract less observed participation where relation discovery and execution are more costly.
core_methodology: The paper employs integer programming to identify optimal arbitrage portfolios across logically related prediction-market contracts. It uses venue metadata and semantic analysis of resolution criteria to identify over 1.9 million logical relations and compiles them into constraint systems.
data_sources: Polymarket order books (full-depth), venue metadata, and semantic analysis of resolution criteria covering more than 255,000 contracts.
alpha_potential: Identifies arbitrage opportunities across prediction markets, with guaranteed profits of 2.2% of committed capital after spreads and fees. The methodology systematically uncovers inefficiencies in cross-market pricing relationships that persist due to discovery and execution costs.
title_cn: 预测市场的组合套利策略
summary_cn: 本研究开发了一个识别和量化预测市场合约间套利机会的框架。通过整数规划分析25.5万份合约间的190万种逻辑关系，模拟执行发现套利组合可确保2.2%的利润空间（税后可达3.2%）。该算法特别擅长发现因关系识别和执行成本高昂而持续存在的套利机会。

title: From Alpha to Execution: Trading Horizons, Regimes, and Schedules under Concave Impact and Hurst Scaling
summary: Classical execution models assume linear impact, diffusive prices, and an exogenous horizon. We study execution under concave power-law impact and Hurst-scaled price fluctuations, and make two contributions. First, we choose the execution horizon by maximizing the Sharpe ratio of the trade's realized P&L. Price moves during the execution window are part of that P&L, so executing more slowly reduces its variance, and because impact is concave it can also lower cost per share. Urgency comes only from alpha realized while the order is being worked. The problem is governed by the signs of two quantities: (i) the duration elasticity of impact $a$, which under a structural prior equals the impact-persistence gap $\beta - H$ and can take either sign; and (ii) the net urgency $\nu$, the rate of alpha realization net of exposure relief. When $\nu$ keeps its sign over the window, an interior optimum exists, to leading order in $T/t_f$, only when both are positive; otherwise the order should be worked at the fastest or slowest admissible pace. In the interior regime the first-order condition involves no impact coefficient, order size or volume, and the objective is flat: for a large-cap example, the window within 1% of maximal Sharpe spans more than an order of magnitude. Second, given the window, we derive the schedule shape by convex programming under an envelope cost. For any increasing per-share cost of delay $w(t)$, the KKT solution is $\phi \propto (\lambda - w(t))_+^{1/\beta}$. For a Hurst-scaled envelope $w \propto t^H$, the normalized schedule depends only on $(\beta, H)$, has a closed form via the incomplete beta function, is front-loaded, and tapers smoothly to zero, saving 10-17% of envelope cost relative to a constant-rate (TWAP) schedule of equal duration. Whether it uses the whole window depends on a single dimensionless robustness level, for which we give a calibration.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an execution optimization framework that combines concave power-law impact models with Hurst-scaled price fluctuations. It provides two key contributions: 1) A methodology for determining optimal execution horizons by maximizing Sharpe ratios of realized P&L, incorporating both alpha decay and impact dynamics; 2) A convex programming approach for deriving optimal schedule shapes under an envelope cost constraint, with closed-form solutions via incomplete beta functions.
data_sources: Implied to require standard market data feeds (tick/by-tick data) for measuring price impact functions and estimating Hurst exponents, likely with execution log data from broker/dealer platforms
alpha_potential: Significant potential for extracting alpha through optimized execution by: 1) Exploiting the concave nature of market impact to reduce costs, 2) Timing execution based on the interaction between alpha decay (ν) and impact duration elasticity (α), 3) Achieving 10-17% cost savings versus TWAP through optimized scheduling
title_cn: 从Alpha到执行：在凹性冲击与赫斯特标度下的交易期限、状态与调度
summary_cn: 本研究提出针对非线性市场冲击与分形波动的执行优化框架，通过夏普比最大化确定最优执行周期，并导出前端加载的最优交易计划。相比TWAP可降低10-17%的执行成本，且领先阶解不依赖于冲击系数或订单规模，对大盘股尤为有效。

title: AlphaBet: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Event Forecasting Agents
summary: Forecasting an unresolved event requires finding relevant evidence and deciding how strongly it supports each outcome. Yet outcome-based training of Large Language Model (LLM) forecasters often begins with preassembled evidence at a single prediction date, leaving evidence acquisition outside the learning loop. We introduce AlphaBet, an agentic reinforcement learning (RL) framework that trains a single LLM policy to search, reason, and report probabilities across multiple pre-resolution dates. Each dated forecast is scored by a proper scoring rule against the eventual outcome, allowing one resolved event to supervise decisions under different information states. We decompose forecasting regret into an evidence-acquisition gap and a probability-reporting gap, and show that Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)'s standard-deviation normalization can distort the reporting target under multi-class proper scores. On GLM-4.5-Air, AlphaBet reduces the Brier score from 0.731 to 0.626 on Forecast-Dojo and from 0.612 to 0.528 on FutureX. Controlled ablations attribute these gains to multi-date training and show that they come from improvements in both information acquisition and probability reporting. Our empirical results validate that GRPO's std normalization degrades proper-scoring-rule performance while leaving top-outcome accuracy largely unchanged.
core_methodology: Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for training Large Language Models (LLMs) to search, reason, and report probabilities across multiple pre-resolution dates, focusing on evidence acquisition and probability reporting.
data_sources: Public forecasting datasets like Forecast-Dojo and FutureX, which involve unresolved events requiring evidence gathering and probability forecasting.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve event-driven trading strategies by enhancing the accuracy of outcome predictions through better evidence acquisition and probability reporting. The framework's ability to learn from multiple pre-resolution dates could be adapted to financial event forecasting (e.g., earnings, macroeconomic announcements).
title_cn: AlphaBet：基于强化学习的大型语言模型事件预测代理
summary_cn: AlphaBet提出了一种强化学习框架，训练单一LLM策略在多日期上搜索证据、推理并报告概率，改进事件预测的准确性和信息获取。其核心方法（如Group Relative Policy Optimization）在金融事件预测（如财报或宏观数据）中具有潜力，可优化量化交易中的事件驱动策略。

title: A Feature Selection Layer Approach for Multi-Class Classification on Neural Networks
summary: In the age of data-driven decision-making, deep learning models have become powerful tools for uncovering patterns and making predictions that influence many aspects of society. However, their broader adoption in scientific and business applications is often limited by a lack of interpretability. Feature weighting methods, which assess the relevance of individual features, are among the most widely studied approaches for improving interpretability. While post hoc techniques have advanced significantly, especially in modeling nuanced relationships between features and labels in multiclass problems, embedded methods typically fall short in this regard. Embedded techniques integrate feature relevance learning directly into the model training process, but they are often unable to capture label-specific relationships. To address the limitation, we propose multiple extensions to the Feature Selection Layer, an embedded feature weighting mechanism for neural networks. Through extensive experimentation, we identify the most effective extension and benchmark it against established feature weighting methods. Our results show that the proposed method matches existing techniques in identifying globally relevant features and outperforms them in capturing label-specific relevance. By leveraging the internal dynamics of the trained neural network, it reveals how individual features contribute to the prediction of specific labels, requiring no post-processing beyond the training process.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an embedded feature weighting mechanism for neural networks called the Feature Selection Layer, with extensions to better capture label-specific relationships in multi-class classification problems. It integrates feature relevance learning directly into model training, eliminating the need for post-processing.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify data sources, but the methodology is applicable to any structured financial datasets (e.g., price/volume data, fundamental data, alternative data) used in neural network-based trading models.
alpha_potential: Improving interpretability in neural networks helps identify which features drive predictions, potentially uncovering more robust factors for trading signals. Label-specific feature relevance could help create class-specific trading signals (e.g., different features for mean-reversion vs. momentum regimes).
title_cn: 用于神经网络多分类的特征选择层方法
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种改进的嵌入式特征选择层方法，可直接在神经网络训练中学习特定类别相关的特征权重，无需后处理。对量化交易的潜在价值在于：1）提升模型可解释性帮助验证因子有效性 2）不同市场状态（如趋势/震荡）可自动选择不同特征组合 3）为多空信号生成提供更透明的决策依据

title: Algorithm Modelization: Transforming Optimization Algorithms into Evolvable Intelligence
summary: Can algorithms be learned and evolved as models, rather than repeatedly redesigned as programs? We explore this question by introducing Algorithm Modelization, a new paradigm that turns iterative algorithms into trainable models. Its central idea is to regard algorithm execution trajectories as computational experience: by learning how algorithmic states evolve over iterations, a model can internalize the knowledge embodied in existing algorithms, reproduce their computational behaviors, and further evolve beyond them through training. As a first realization of this paradigm, we modelize iterative optimization as an autoregressive process, where preceding generations constitute the computational context for generating the next population. We develop a dimension-independent population-temporal architecture to capture both population interactions and iterative dynamics, together with an imitation-to-surpassing learning framework that first acquires algorithmic knowledge from heterogeneous teachers and then improves the resulting optimizer directly through optimization feedback. The modelized optimizer consequently goes beyond reproducing individual algorithms: it consolidates heterogeneous search knowledge into a single trainable model, achieves stronger optimization capability through subsequent improvement, and generalizes its acquired knowledge across problems and substantially larger unseen dimensions. More fundamentally, Algorithm Modelization makes algorithmic capability accumulable through learning, where new algorithms and problem-solving experience can become training resources for progressively improving the model. Our results establish a promising path from manually designed algorithms toward general algorithm models that learn, generalize, and evolve from computational experience.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Algorithm Modelization, a paradigm that transforms traditional optimization algorithms into trainable models by learning from algorithmic execution trajectories. It models iterative optimization as an autoregressive process, capturing population interactions and iterative dynamics through a dimension-independent architecture. The methodology includes an imitation-to-surpassing learning framework that first imitates heterogeneous algorithmic teachers and then improves the optimizer through direct optimization feedback.
data_sources: The methodology is generic and can be applied to any optimization problem, including those in quantitative finance such as portfolio optimization, parameter tuning for trading strategies, or risk management.
alpha_potential: The approach could enable the development of more robust and adaptive optimization algorithms for trading strategies, potentially uncovering more efficient portfolio allocations or better parameter settings for algorithmic trading models. The ability to generalize across problems and dimensions suggests potential for creating more flexible and scalable trading systems.
title_cn: 算法模型化：将优化算法转化为可进化的智能
summary_cn: 该论文提出的算法模型化新范式，通过将优化算法转化为可训练的模型，可学习算法执行轨迹并进化。此方法在量化交易中具有潜力，可用于改进投资组合优化、交易策略参数调整等，通过整合异构搜索知识和优化反馈，提升算法在金融应用中的适应性和泛化能力。

title: Non-Parametric Optimization for Scalable Learning in Stochastic Decision Problems
summary: Stochastic optimization (SO) plays a central role in decision-making under uncertainty. Among SO problems, time-varying stochastic optimization (TV-SO) is particularly important due to its applications in adaptive control and machine learning. Non-parametric approaches have been proposed for time-varying deterministic optimization; however, they have not been developed for their stochastic counterparts. This work addresses that gap by developing a stochastic variational framework based on Malliavin calculus. This framework yields non-parametric optimality conditions for SO problems with stochastic decisions and supports the design of a scalable deep-learning algorithm that is insensitive to the parameterization dimension. This algorithm, called the Stochastic Path Follower (SPF), is applied to two important problems under distribution drift, namely least-squares recovery and logistic regression. Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art learning-based and gradient-based methods in both performance and scalability.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a stochastic variational framework based on Malliavin calculus for time-varying stochastic optimization (TV-SO). It proposes the Stochastic Path Follower (SPF) algorithm, a non-parametric approach for solving SO problems under distribution drift, applied to least-squares recovery and logistic regression.
data_sources: The methodology is general and can be applied to various financial time series data, including stock prices, market indices, and other economic indicators that exhibit non-stationary behavior or distribution drift.
alpha_potential: The SPF algorithm's ability to handle time-varying distributions and non-stationarities in data could be leveraged to develop trading strategies that adapt to changing market conditions, potentially uncovering alpha in markets with regime shifts or structural breaks.
title_cn: 随机决策问题中可扩展学习的非参数优化方法
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种基于Malliavin微积分的随机变分框架，用于解决时变随机优化问题。开发的随机路径跟随算法(SPF)能够有效处理分布漂移，在最小二乘恢复和逻辑回归中优于现有方法。该技术可应用于金融时间序列的非平稳性处理，为适应市场状态变化的量化交易策略提供理论基础。

title: OliO: ODE-based Linear Transition Operator for Self-Supervised Time Series Forecasting
summary: Self-supervised representation learning has advanced time series forecasting by capturing robust features from unlabeled data. However, existing contrastive and masking-based methods often struggle to explicitly model the underlying temporal flow, either by treating time lag as noise or by disrupting the inherent temporal dynamics essential for forecasting. To address these limitations, we propose OliO (**O**DE-based **Li**near Transition **O**perator), a plug-and-play self-supervised learning method that learns bidirectional temporal flows as a continuous and structurally consistent dynamical system. OliO introduces a transition operator derived from linear Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) to align latent representations across arbitrary time shifts. By imposing a strictly upper triangular constraint on the transition matrix, we mathematically ensure numerical stability and enforce a robust polynomial boundary that effectively captures long-term dependencies while preventing the exponential divergence typically found in unconstrained ODE-based models. This structural constraint induces a temporally coherent representation space that preserves the underlying flow essential for accurate forecasting. Extensive experiments across various backbone architectures and benchmarks demonstrate that OliO achieves significant performance gains, providing Mean Squared Error (MSE) reductions of up to 5.75% over the most competitive grid-searched SOTA baselines. The code is available at *https://github.com/eai-lab/OliO*
core_methodology: OliO introduces a self-supervised learning method based on linear Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) to model bidirectional temporal flows in time series data. It uses a strictly upper triangular transition matrix to ensure numerical stability and capture long-term dependencies while preventing exponential divergence.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial datasets, but the methodology is applicable to any time series data, including stock prices, market indices, or other financial time series.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to capture long-term dependencies and maintain temporal coherence could be valuable for predicting financial time series, potentially uncovering hidden patterns or trends that are not captured by traditional models. This could lead to improved forecasting accuracy in trading strategies.

summary_cn: OliO提出了一种基于线性常微分方程的自监督学习方法，通过严格上三角约束的转移矩阵建模双向时间流，确保数值稳定性并捕捉长期依赖关系。在金融时间序列预测中，该方法可能提高预测准确性，为量化交易策略提供新的信号来源。

title: Perceive, Solve, Reason: Progressive Capability Formation in Time Series-LLMs
summary: Large language models (LLMs) can now perceive, describe, and reason about images and audio, yet time series understanding remains underestimated: most work uses LLMs as forecasters and classifiers, reasoning studies are few and narrow, and no suite trains and evaluates the full range of capabilities. In this paper, we build the first such suite, with 337K training and 44K evaluation samples across three progressive capabilities, Perceive, Solve, and Reason, and use it to ask how time series should enter an LLM that must master all three, and in what order. We find that a dedicated encoder is essential: with one, a 4B model surpasses GPT-4o on every perception attribute we test, whereas textualizing the series costs 8--10 points in reasoning accuracy. The capabilities then build on one another: learning them in order beats mixing the same data and rivals reasoning-only training with over three times the reasoning data, but only when an encoder is used. Analyses further reveal that capabilities are transferred through distinct network depths rather than simply stacked, and that a stage converged on its own benchmark is not necessarily ready for the next. Distilled into a simple recipe, these findings yield 4B TS-LLMs that, without any target-domain data, outperform four recent 7B TS-LLMs on seven of eight out-of-domain metrics, by up to 11 points. We therefore advocate treating time series as a first-class modality for LLMs, read through dedicated encoders and taught to perceive before they reason.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a comprehensive suite for training and evaluating large language models (LLMs) on time series data, focusing on three progressive capabilities: Perceive, Solve, and Reason. It emphasizes the importance of a dedicated encoder for time series inputs and the sequential learning of these capabilities for optimal performance.
data_sources: The study uses a dataset with 337K training and 44K evaluation samples across various time series tasks, likely including synthetic and real-world time series data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be applied to financial time series data (e.g., stock prices, economic indicators) to enhance forecasting, anomaly detection, and reasoning about market conditions. The superior performance of a 4B model with a dedicated encoder suggests potential for extracting unique signals from time series data.
title_cn: 感知、解决、推理：时间序列-大语言模型中的渐进能力形成
summary_cn: 该研究构建了一个全面的时间序列-大语言模型训练与评估套件，强调专用编码器和渐进式学习（感知→解决→推理）对性能的关键提升。在金融应用中，该方法可优化时间序列预测、市场状态推理和异常检测，4B模型表现优于更大模型，表明其在高频交易和量化策略中的潜在优势。

title: LagNet: Lag-Structured Operators for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
summary: Long-term time series forecasting maps a finite history window to an extended future horizon. Many existing models focus primarily on the design of input representations and model structures, while paying less attention to the structural form of the history-to-future forecasting operator itself. We examine this operator directly and find that, across model families, sensitivity matrices exhibit recurring diagonal patterns whose diagonals correspond to relative temporal lags. Motivated by this observation, we develop a framework for direct multi-step forecasting based on lag-structured temporal operators. Its basic building block, LagLayer, constructs a Toeplitz matrix by tying history-to-future connections with the same relative lag and incorporates horizon-wise and history-wise scaling coefficients to relax exact sharing. This design enables LagLayer to serve as an effective replacement for temporal linear layers in existing forecasting models. Stacking LagLayer modules with activations and multiple feature maps yields LagNet. Experiments on long-term time series forecasting benchmarks show that our method is competitive with strong baselines, while sensitivity matrix diagnostics and limited-data experiments demonstrate that LagLayer provides an effective and sample-efficient alternative to a linear layer.
core_methodology: Direct multi-step forecasting using lag-structured temporal operators (LagLayer) that construct a Toeplitz matrix to tie history-to-future connections with the same relative lag, incorporating horizon-wise and history-wise scaling coefficients.
data_sources: Generic time series data, likely applicable to financial time series like stock prices, volatility, or macroeconomic indicators.
alpha_potential: Potential for capturing momentum effects or regime changes in financial markets through improved multi-horizon prediction of time series patterns.
title_cn: LagNet：用于长期时间序列预测的滞后结构算子
summary_cn: 该论文提出的LagNet框架通过滞后结构算子改善了长期时间序列预测能力，对量化交易中的多周期价格预测和风险模型优化具有实用价值。其Toeplitz矩阵设计可有效捕捉金融市场中的动量效应和周期性模式。

title: Reading the News Without Hindsight: NoLBERT Topics and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
summary: Language models that read financial news are usually trained on text from the same years used to test them, so a backtest can reward hindsight. We build news topics from NoLBERT, an encoder pretrained only on text published between 1976 and 1995, adapted into a sentence encoder by contrastive fine-tuning on passages of the same article, with no labels or returns. We compare it with LDA, MiniLM and FinBERT readers on 1.26 million articles from 2012 to 2024, convert each reader's topics into attention shocks and stock exposures, and forecast the returns of the 1,000 largest US stocks with eight models at three rebalancing frequencies. Models are fitted on 2013-2019, choices are made on 2020-2021, and 2022-2024 is held out. The experiment with the best validation score loses money at every frequency. Measuring attention shocks against the past 63 trading days instead of 5 raises the test rank IC of every reader. NoLBERT gives the most stable topics and forecasts about as well as LDA. An equal-weight combination of all readers and models earns a monthly net Sharpe ratio of 1.12, significant against zero before adjusting for the search but not against a price-only benchmark.
core_methodology: The paper introduces NoLBERT, a language model pre-trained on financial news from 1976-1995 and fine-tuned via contrastive learning (without using labels or returns data). It compares NoLBERT with LDA, MiniLM, and FinBERT in generating news topics, which are then converted into attention shocks and stock exposures for return forecasting. The methodology involves out-of-sample testing with a clear temporal split (training on 2013-2019, validation on 2020-2021, and testing on 2022-2024).
data_sources: 1.26 million financial news articles from 2012 to 2024, focusing on the 1,000 largest US stocks.
alpha_potential: The paper demonstrates that combining multiple readers (NoLBERT, LDA, MiniLM, FinBERT) and models can yield a monthly net Sharpe ratio of 1.12, though the significance is limited when adjusted for multiple testing or compared to price-only benchmarks. The key insight is that using longer-term attention shocks (63-day vs. 5-day) improves the test rank IC, suggesting potential alpha in news-based momentum signals.
title_cn: 无需后见之明阅读新闻：NoLBERT主题与股票横截面收益

title: Conformal Policy Selection: When to Deploy AI Decisions for Targeted Intervention
summary: Artificial-intelligence (AI) policies are increasingly used to make consequential decisions in medicine, finance, education, and public services, yet deploying them responsibly requires knowing not only whether a policy helps on average, but for whom. Existing tools for off-policy evaluation and safe policy learning provide population-level guarantees, but some individuals may experience adverse treatment effects. We recast targeted deployment as a multiple-testing problem: for each candidate unit, test whether the outcome under the AI policy would exceed a user-specified threshold, and control the false discovery rate (FDR) among the selected set. Our method, Conformal Policy Selection, combines weighted conformal $p$-values that account for the distributional shift from behavior to target policy with a two-step selection-and-pruning procedure. We prove finite-sample FDR control and establish a doubly robust asymptotic guarantee, where FDR remains controlled if either the outcome model or the propensity model is correctly specified. Synthetic experiments verify these guarantees across four misspecification regimes, and a semi-synthetic study built on real electronic-health-record covariates illustrates how the same FDR control can act as a deployment safety gate, bounding the harmful treatments that a globally trained policy would otherwise administer to a high-risk subpopulation where it misgeneralizes. The framework offers a principled method for safe AI deployment in high-stakes applications.
core_methodology: Combines weighted conformal p-values to account for distributional shifts between behavior and target policies with a two-step selection-and-pruning procedure for false discovery rate (FDR) control
data_sources: Theoretical framework tested with synthetic experiments and semi-synthetic data built on real electronic health records (shown in medical context, but method is domain-agnostic)
alpha_potential: Enables targeted deployment of algorithmic strategies by identifying subgroups where the strategy works (avoiding misapplication), potentially improving strategy profitability by avoiding losses from misgeneralized signals
title_cn: 合规策略选择：何时部署AI决策以实现精准干预
summary_cn: 该方法通过控制错误发现率(FDR)，为AI交易策略的精准部署提供安全边界。结合加权合规p值和双重鲁棒性保障，可在市场不同状态（如不同波动机制）下识别策略有效子群体，避免将错误信号应用于不适用市场环境，提升策略稳健性。

title: Neural Operators Which Certifiably Simultaneously Solve Infinitely Many Convex Programs using Logarithmic Rank and Linear Complexity
summary: Neural operators (NOs) are a class of deep learning models designed to simultaneously solve infinitely many related problems by casting them into an infinite-dimensional space, whereon these NOs operate. Such operator learning problems arise naturally in mathematical finance, for instance, when learning families of optimal portfolios or hedging strategies. Two significant gaps, however, remain between theory and practice: 1) most universal approximation guarantees do not describe practically implementable NOs or are pure existence statements; and 2) worst-case parameter bounds from universal approximation theorems suggest that constructed NOs may require an unrealistically large number of parameters to solve most operator learning problems, which stands in direct opposition to a slew of experimental evidence. This paper closes these gaps by exhibiting a short and simple training algorithm to construct a specific class of NOs, proximal equilibrium operators (PEOs), using (realistic) finite-dimensional deep equilibrium layers to solve families of convex optimization problems over a separable Hilbert space $X$. Here, the inputs are smooth, convex loss functions on $X$, and the outputs are the associated (approximate) solutions to the optimization problems defined by each input loss. Our main result is a certificate showing that, when the input losses lie in a suitable infinite-dimensional set, our PEOs trained with our algorithm do in fact uniformly approximate the corresponding solutions to arbitrary precision, with rank and width growing only logarithmically and the depth growing linearly in the reciprocal of the approximation error. We then validate both our theoretical results and the trainability of PEOs on three applications: non-linear PDEs, stochastic optimal control, and portfolio optimization and hedging problems in mathematical finance.
core_methodology: Proximal Equilibrium Operators (PEOs) using deep equilibrium layers to solve families of convex optimization problems over a separable Hilbert space, with inputs as smooth, convex loss functions and outputs as approximate solutions to the optimization problems.
data_sources: Theoretical framework for solving convex optimization problems, with applications to portfolio optimization and hedging problems. Specific market data sources are not mentioned but implied to be generic financial data.
alpha_potential: Potential for optimizing portfolios and hedging strategies by learning families of optimal solutions simultaneously, which can lead to more efficient and robust trading strategies.

summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种基于近端平衡算子（PEO）的神经算子方法，可同时求解无限多凸优化问题。该方法在数学金融中的应用包括学习最优投资组合和对冲策略家族，提高了策略的效率和鲁棒性。理论认证和实验验证显示，该方法在非线性PDE、随机最优控制和投资组合优化中均有效。

title: Empirical Bayesian Multi-Bandit Learning
summary: Multi-task learning in contextual bandits has attracted significant research interest due to its potential to enhance decision-making across multiple related tasks by leveraging shared structures and task-specific heterogeneity. In this article, we propose a novel hierarchical Bayesian framework for learning in various bandit instances. This framework captures both the heterogeneity and the correlations among different bandit instances through a hierarchical Bayesian model, enabling effective information sharing while accommodating instance-specific variations. Unlike previous methods that overlook the learning of the covariance structure across bandits, we introduce an empirical Bayesian approach to estimate the covariance matrix of the prior distribution. This enhances both the practicality and flexibility of learning across multi-bandits. Building on this approach, we develop two efficient algorithms: ebmTS (Empirical Bayesian Multi-Bandit Thompson Sampling) and ebmUCB (Empirical Bayesian Multi-Bandit Upper Confidence Bound), both of which incorporate the estimated prior into the decision-making process. We provide the frequentist regret upper bounds for the proposed algorithms, thereby filling a research gap in the field of multi-bandit problems. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our algorithms, particularly in complex environments. Our methods achieve lower cumulative regret compared to existing techniques, highlighting their effectiveness in balancing exploration and exploitation across multi-bandits.
core_methodology: Hierarchical Bayesian framework for multi-bandit learning, with empirical Bayesian estimation of covariance matrix. Algorithms include Thompson Sampling (ebmTS) and Upper Confidence Bound (ebmUCB) variants customized for multi-bandit scenarios.
data_sources: Tested on both synthetic datasets and real-world datasets (unspecified domain but methodology applicable to financial time-series data)
alpha_potential: Enables adaptive dynamic asset allocation across correlated instruments by: 1) Learning hidden relationships among trading arms (assets) 2) Optimizing exploration-exploitation tradeoff in volatile markets 3) Transferring knowledge across related trading strategies

title: Learning Agentic Time Series Forecasting via Trajectory Distillation and Memory-Based Reinforcement Learning
summary: Recent agentic time series forecasting (TSF) approaches use large language models (LLMs) to autonomously orchestrate analytical and forecasting tools and reason about temporal patterns using the resulting evidence. However, many such approaches rely on powerful LLMs in training-free, prompt-driven workflows, leaving open whether smaller models can learn these interaction and reasoning capabilities. In this paper, we introduce Cast-R1, an 8Bparameter agentic forecasting model trained through trajectory distillation and multi-turn reinforcement learning with structured memory. First, we develop a forecasting agent harness with specialized analysis and prediction tools to generate multi-turn interaction trajectories using a teacher LLM, which are subsequently evaluated and selected for supervised fine-tuning. Second, we apply group relative policy optimization (GRPO) across multi-turn forecasting episodes, with structured memory preserving diagnostic evidence and intermediate forecasts for state construction. Rewards based on prediction accuracy and temporal structure guide tool selection, model routing, and forecast refinement. A difficulty-aware curriculum combines sample filtering and progressive sample ordering during training. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of Cast-R1. These findings highlight the potential of forecasting-specific post-training to equip smaller LLMs with multi-turn, tool-augmented forecasting capabilities within structured workflows.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Cast-R1, an 8B-parameter agentic forecasting model trained via trajectory distillation and multi-turn reinforcement learning with structured memory. It utilizes a forecasting agent harness with specialized tools to generate interaction trajectories using a teacher LLM, followed by supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with GRPO. The model's state construction is supported by structured memory, and rewards based on prediction accuracy and temporal structure guide tool selection and forecast refinement.
data_sources: The abstract mentions extensive experiments on multiple datasets, though specific financial datasets are not detailed. The methodology suggests potential applicability to time series data common in financial markets (e.g., stock prices, economic indicators).
alpha_potential: The approach could uncover complex temporal patterns in financial time series data, potentially generating alpha through improved forecasting accuracy and adaptive tool selection. The structured memory and multi-turn interaction may capture nuanced market dynamics not easily modeled by traditional methods.
title_cn: 通过轨迹蒸馏和基于记忆的强化学习实现自主时间序列预测

title: Adaptive Conditional Residual Sampling for Spectral Risk Optimisation under Decision-Dependent Uncertainty
summary: We consider minimising a spectral risk objective, the expected cost plus a weighted conditional value-at-risk, when the distribution of the uncertain parameters depends on the decision and can only be sampled through a stochastic simulator under a fixed budget of draws. We propose adaptive conditional residual sampling (ACRS). It takes one simulator draw at each point of a space-filling design, fits a heteroscedastic regression model of the decision-dependent distribution and reuses the standardised residual vectors as scenarios to construct a deterministic surrogate. ACRS searches this surrogate for several local optima, adds draws around the most promising ones, ranks the candidates on the simulator with common random numbers and finishes with sample-path local refinement using tail importance sampling. We show that the optimality gap of the surrogate minimiser is bounded by the Wasserstein error of the scenario distribution and that the refinement estimator is consistent. In the experiments, all methods share the budget accounting, the design sampler and the local refinement routine, and solutions are scored by normalised regret against reference optima. On 60 random instances of an analytic family with a closed-form objective, ACRS attains a mean regret of 11.8% against 22.3-42.3% for Bayesian optimisation, cross-entropy, kernel-density, stochastic-gradient and refinement-only baselines; its lead is largest at small budgets and, relative to the kernel-density method, tends to grow with the dimension. ACRS also has the lowest mean regret on two six-dimensional benchmarks and three development problems, and performs comparably to pure local refinement on three held-out problems frozen before testing.
core_methodology: Adaptive conditional residual sampling (ACRS) for optimizing spectral risk objectives under decision-dependent uncertainty. The method involves heteroscedastic regression modeling and scenario construction using standardized residuals, followed by local optimization and tail importance sampling.
data_sources: Stochastic simulator outputs representing uncertain decision-dependent parameters (could be applied to financial market simulations or risk scenarios).
alpha_potential: Potential for improving portfolio risk optimization and tail-risk management strategies by more accurately capturing decision-dependent uncertainties and conditional value-at-risk.
